test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (JSO) 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Using usual notations, the correlation coefficient between two random variables, X and Y, is given by:

options.text: r(X, Y) = Cov(X, Y) - σX σY
r(X, Y) = Cov(X, Y) + σX σY

solution:
The correct answer is** r(X,Y) = (Cov(X,Y))/(sigma_X sigma_Y )**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** Correlation Coefficient:

__
 
• r(X,Y) = (Cov(X,Y))/(sigma_X sigma_Y ) is the correct formula for the correlation coefficient.
 
• It standardizes the covariance by dividing it by the product of the standard deviations of X and Y.
 
• **This formula ensures that the correlation coefficient lies between -1 and 1.**
 
• It measures the strength and direction of the linear relationship between two variables.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 Explanation of Incorrect Options:

 
• **Option 1:** r(X, Y) = Cov(X, Y) - σX σY

 
 
• This option incorrectly subtracts the product of the standard deviations from the covariance.
 
• It does not provide a standardized measure of correlation.
 
• The result can fall outside the range of -1 to 1.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** r(X, Y) = Cov(X, Y) + σX σY
 
 
• This option incorrectly adds the product of the standard deviations to the covariance.
 
• It also fails to standardize the covariance.
 
• This formula can yield values outside the acceptable range for correlation coefficients.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** r(X, Y) = (sigma_Xsigma_Y)/(Cov(X,Y))
 
 
• This option incorrectly inverts the relationship by dividing the product of the standard deviations by the covariance.
 
• It does not provide a meaningful measure of correlation.
 
• The values obtained from this formula are not constrained between -1 and 1.
